statements.text: Permits are available through municipalities accredited to administer the Safety Codes Act and through agencies serving non-accredited municipalities.
SCC IB 2026-10-16: Authority Having Jurisdiction rests with accredited organizations and the Alberta Safety Codes Authority; an individual SCO is not the AHJ.

provincial_facts.text: Alberta.ca: permits are available through municipalities accredited to administer the Safety Codes Act and through agencies serving non-accredited municipalities; ASCA (a Council division) oversees agencies in non-accredited areas.
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 26(1) On the application of a local authority, the Minister may, by order
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 27(1) On the application of a regional services commission
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 28(1) On the application of a corporation an Administrator may,
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 30(1) On the application of a person, an Administrator may,
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 30.1(1) On the order of the Minister, the Council shall establish a division of the Council
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 38(1) An Administrator or a safety codes officer may issue a written variance
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): A safety codes officer on issuing a variance shall notify an Administrator.
Safety Codes Act text (QP consolidation): 66(1) Except as provided in this section, a bylaw of a municipality that purports to regulate

SCC IB 2026-10-16 says municipalities and regional services commissions are designated as accredited 'by the Administrator of Accreditation' (ss. 26-27). The Act text retrieved says the Minister designates them by order (s.26(1), s.27(1)); discrepancy recorded, not resolved.

SCC IB 2025-11-18 (mandatory documentation of variances): building, fire and plumbing variances must document alternative solutions per Division C of the applicable code (Division C 2.3.1); electrical, gas and private sewage rely on QMP/QMS equivalency documentation; each variance copied to the Council within 10 days; supporting documentation retained and produced on request by an Administrator.
SCC IB 2025-11-18: submit a copy of each variance to the Safety Codes Council within 10 days of issuance.
SCC IB 2026-10-01: effective December 1, 2026 the Orders and Variances Portal (OVP) becomes the sole acceptable method for registering orders and variances; only SCOs can register.
SCC variances page: under s.38 an Administrator must be notified of variances; OVP becomes the sole acceptable registration method effective December 1, 2026.
SCC IB 2024-03-01: National Building Code - 2023 Alberta Edition comes into force May 1, 2024 (edition printing not stated in this bulletin).

accreditation_model.note: Per SCC IB 2026-10-16, NBC-AE 2023 Division A 1.4.1.2 (which defines AHJ as a building SCO) must be read functionally: the AHJ is the accredited organization (or ASCA) and the SCO is the delegated officer. This is the bulletin's position; the NBC clause itself was not checked here.

facts.text: Alberta.ca: municipalities accredited to administer the Safety Codes Act issue permits; agencies serve non-accredited municipalities under ASCA oversight.
SCC IB 2026-10-16: authority having jurisdiction rests with accredited organizations and the Alberta Safety Codes Authority; SCOs exercise delegated powers and do not replace the AHJ.

Calgary variance route per city guide: owner or agent applies to a safety codes officer in the building discipline; the Request for Specific Variance form is required; applications are reviewed within Inspections & Permit Services; a variance can only be accepted once a building permit has been applied for.
Calgary guide: the application and documentation will be reviewed by the applicable parties within Inspections & Permit Services.
Calgary guide: a variance request can only be accepted if a building permit has been applied for, because a variance must be tied to a building permit.

facts.text: Safety Codes Permit Bylaw 15894 (consolidated January 1, 2016) recites that under section 66 of the Safety Codes Act an accredited municipality may make bylaws for permits.
Bylaw 15894: a person shall not start an undertaking requiring a permit under the bylaw unless a permit has been issued.
Bylaw 15894: the City Manager shall issue a permit where the undertaking meets the requirements of the Safety Codes Act.

Edmonton guideline (COE-IM-GUIDE-0040 v01, 2025-04-15): alternative solutions that impact emergency response are subject to peer review by Safety Codes, Permits and Inspections (SCPI) and Edmonton Fire Rescue Services (EFRS), and may be evaluated as part of the building permit application.

Edmonton house-permit requirements page: 'Policy Solutions' section says the building permit office offers policy solutions for conditions that repeatedly require a variance to NBC(AE) prescriptive requirements (B14-01, B14-01G, B19-03 archived, B19-04, B23-01, B23-02, Bulletin B23-03, Interpretation B23-05).

Edmonton Search of Records: a request examines Development Services Records and Community Standards Investigations files and can retrieve filed property records or plans such as mechanical drawings and floor plans; 2026 application fee $120 per titled lot search; photocopies $0.25 per 8 x 11 page.
Edmonton Search of Records: no commercial building plans on record before 1977 or residential building plans before 1985.

access_gaps: No official municipal-website list was retrieved for the 328 non-priority municipalities. Future scraping needs a source of official websites or a per-municipality discovery step.

Drawings and technical files are not self-serve: Calgary provides plans and records on request; Edmonton provides filed plans through the paid Search of Records request, with date cut-offs (pre-1977 commercial; pre-1985 residential).
Open-data permit datasets (Calgary c2es-76ed, Edmonton 24uj-dj8v) carry no drawing attachments; Calgary's includes applicant and contractor names.
Calgary and Edmonton open-data portal HTML is a JavaScript shell; dataset metadata was taken from the Socrata views API and records were not sampled.
The Orders and Variances Portal (OVP) becomes the sole registration route from 2026-12-01; public access to variance registry entries was not verified.
The SCC Accreditation Search returns organization rows only: no service-area boundaries, no per-organization website, and the Site List reports linked from the rows were not fetched.
The Safety Codes Act text retrieved is a QP PDF consolidation; its in-force date was not verified before citing.
Edmonton Permit Bylaw 15894 is a 2016 consolidation; currency not verified.
The SCC IB 2026-10-16 says municipalities are designated by the Administrator (ss.26-27); the Act text retrieved says the Minister designates by order. Recorded as a discrepancy.
Appeal-decision PDFs (83 linked on the saved index) are owned by L06 and A06; no duplicate download was made here.
L04 holds a Calgary advisory B23-006 (fourplex emergency access) that is not on the saved current advisories page (B23-006 absent from the 13 listed). Possibly withdrawn or superseded; not confirmed.

City of Lloydminster (Alberta side) has no SCC accreditation listed in any discipline. The ASCA page lists a Superior Safety Codes 'Lloydminster Office'; whether it serves the Alberta side is not stated and was not confirmed.
Municipality of Jasper is listed by SCC for Fire only (no Building accreditation in the snapshot). Who issues Building permits there was not verified.

The SCC snapshot has 39 municipal-type roster rows accredited for other disciplines only and 36 with no SCC accreditation listed; the SCC Building list alone therefore does not describe full AHJ coverage.
